:::{#exm-canonical-score}
#### Score of a logistic model

Logistic regression uses the canonical link for a Bernoulli outcome
(@exm-canonical-links), with $\phi = 1$,
so @eq-canonical-score applies.
Take $n = 3$ observations
with $\vx_i = \tp{(1, x_i)}$,
$x = (0, 1, 2)$ and $y = (0, 1, 1)$,
and evaluate the score at $\vb = \tp{(0, 1)}$.
The fitted means are
$\mu_i = \expit(\b_0 + \b_1 x_i) = \expit(x_i)$:

| $i$ | $x_i$ | $y_i$ | $\mu_i$ | $y_i - \mu_i$ |
|-----|-------|-------|---------|---------------|
| 1   | 0     | 0     | 0.5000  | -0.5000       |
| 2   | 1     | 1     | 0.7311  | 0.2689        |
| 3   | 2     | 1     | 0.8808  | 0.1192        |

Then:

$$
\ba
\scorev\paren{\tp{(0, 1)}}
&= \sum_{i=1}^3 \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ x_i \end{pmatrix} (y_i - \mu_i)
&& \text{(canonical-link score, with } \phi = 1\text{)}
\\ &= \begin{pmatrix} -0.5000 + 0.2689 + 0.1192 \\ 0 \cdot (-0.5000) + 1 \cdot 0.2689 + 2 \cdot 0.1192 \end{pmatrix}
&& \text{(substitute the table)}
\\ &= \begin{pmatrix} -0.1119 \\ 0.5073 \end{pmatrix}
&& \text{(add)}
\ea
$$

The second component is positive,
so increasing $\b_1$ from 1 would increase the log-likelihood.
:::

::: notes
The [logistic regression chapter](logistic-regression.qmd#thm-logistic-score-fn)
derives this score directly from the Bernoulli likelihood,
and the [Poisson score exercise](count-regression.qmd#exr-prac-glm-score)
gives the same form for the log link.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-noncanonical-score}
#### Score of a Poisson model with the identity link (counterexample)

With a non-canonical link, @eq-canonical-score need not hold.
Take a Poisson outcome with the identity link,
so $\mu_i = \tp{\vx_i}\vb$.
The log-likelihood contribution is
$\llik_i = y_i \logf{\mu_i} - \mu_i - \logf{y_i!}$, so:

$$
\ba
\deriv{\vb} \llik_i
&= \deriv{\vb}\mu_i \cdot \deriv{\mu_i}\llik_i
&& \text{(chain rule)}
\\ &= \vx_i \paren{\frac{y_i}{\mu_i} - 1}
&& \text{(differentiate each factor)}
\\ &= \vx_i \frac{y_i - \mu_i}{\mu_i}
&& \text{(common denominator)}
\ea
$$

Each residual is divided by $\mu_i$.
For instance, take $\vb = \tp{(1, 1)}$, $x = (0, 1)$, and $y = (2, 1)$,
so $\mu = (1, 2)$.
The correct score is
$\tp{(1, 0)} \cdot \frac{1}{1} + \tp{(1, 1)} \cdot \frac{-1}{2} = \tp{(0.5, -0.5)}$,
whereas @eq-canonical-score would give
$\tp{(1, 0)} \cdot 1 + \tp{(1, 1)} \cdot (-1) = \tp{(0, -1)}$.
:::
